newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER SHOWCASE-ROMA V JUVENTUS - MATCH ANALYSIS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-ROMA V JUVENTUS - MATCH ANALYSIS.

text.p: Here is an analysis of the strengths and weaknesses of Roma and Juventus who meet in Italy's serie A at the Olympic Stadium on Saturday (1830 GMT):

Playing style: Argentine coach Carlos Bianchi, six league matches into his new job, has a "Jekyll and Hyde" team -- capable of beating champions Milan 3-0 two weeks ago and then losing 2-0 to bottom of the table Verona last weekend. Consistency and discipline are missing.
Bianchi has so far stuck with a 4-4-2 formation but may experiment after two successive defeats. Roma are heavily South American-influenced and have great flair but not much unity.

Strengths: Strong in attack with experienced Argentine Abel Balbo, Uruguayan Daniel Fonseca and young Italians Francesco Totti and Marco Delvecchio the target men. Roma made an astute summer signing by buying new Italian squad member Damiano Tommasi who is living up to his promise.

Weaknesses: Roma bought few players over the summer and lack a truly outstanding playmaker who could turn a good team into an exceptional one. Midfield looks shaky and depends heavily on steady Swedish star Jonas Thern being fit. Young goalkeeper Giorgio Sterchele lacks serie A experience. Argentine defender Roberto Trotta is homesick and has been sent home.

Motivation: Players smarting from consecutive defeats. Roma beat champions Milan 3-0 in last home match and, after euphoria of that win, will want Juventus scalp to provide similar springboard. Bianchi will have been encouraged by third division Nocerina holding Juventus to a 0-0 draw in the Italian Cup third round on Wednesday. Starting as underdogs will help. A win will put them back up with the leaders. Defeat, followed by likely elimination from UEFA Cup, could threaten Bianchi.

Line-up (from): Giorgio Sterchele; Aldair, Fabio Petruzzi, Enrico Annoni, Marco Lanna, Damiano Tommasi, Jonas Thern, Francesco Statuto, Francesco Moriero, Massimiliano Cappioli, Abel Balbo, Daniel Fonseca, Marco Delvecchio, Francesco Totti.

Playing style: Coach Marcello Lippi favoured the "Tridente" -- a three-pronged attack -- early in the season but switched to 4-4-2 after forward Alessandro del Piero was injured in September. With del Piero back on Wednesday, he reverted to 4-3-3 while resting top players. Expect French midfielder Zinedine Zidane to fall back into a deeper midfield role than recently if Lippi sticks with 4-3-3.

Strengths: In depth, with talented squad allowing regular rotation. Croat Alen Boksic and Zidane have stepped comfortably into shoes of Gianluca Vialli and Fabrizio Ravanelli. Full of top internationals, Juventus also enjoy stability with Lippi the sole current serie A coach to have won the title before.

Weaknesses: Boksic regularly squanders a fistful of chances, Zidane was strangely subdued in the opening matches and his true class only now beginning to emerge. Captain and Italian international Antonio Conte is injured. Del Piero clearly suffering from long layoff and needs matches.

Motivation: The same that applies to all league leaders and European Cup holders -- get ahead and stay ahead. Their 2-0 win against rivals Inter -- a team tipped by many for the title -- last weekend gave Juventus a major boost. Wednesday's draw against Nocerina should ward off any complacency.

Line-up (probably from): Angelo Peruzzi; Moreno Torricelli, Gianluca Pessotto, Ciro Ferrara, Paolo Montero, Angelo Di Livio, Didier Deschamps, Zinedine Zidane, Vladimir Jugovic, Michele Padovano, Alessandro del Piero, Alen Boksic.
